description: runs() is a set of strings: = and ≠ compare two of them, ⊆ and ⊈ test one in another, ∖ takes their difference, and ∈ and ∉ test a string in one. The alternative bad fails, since its runs differ (engine §5, §10).
grammar:
%rule text good | bad
%rule good $a(W) $b(W) $c(W)
%conditions runs($a) = runs($b), runs($a) ≠ runs($c), runs($a) ⊆ runs($c), runs($c) ⊈ runs($a), runs($c) ∖ runs($a) ≠ ∅, runs($b) ∖ runs($a) = ∅, "do" ∈ runs($c), "do" ∉ runs($a)
%rule bad $d(W) $e(W) $f(W)
%conditions runs($d) = runs($f)
